## Classes

### <a name="proxmox_datacenter_manager"></a>`proxmox_datacenter_manager`

Writes the PDM API connection settings to a YAML transport file. Declare this class
before classes that contain `pdm_*` resources so providers can discover the transport
before they retrieve existing resources.

#### Examples

##### Configure a PDM connection

```puppet
class { 'proxmox_datacenter_manager':
  host         => 'pdm.example.com',
  token_id     => 'puppet@pdm!puppet',
  token_secret => Sensitive(lookup('pdm::token_secret')),
  ssl_ca_file  => '/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem',
}
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `proxmox_datacenter_manager` class:

* [`token_id`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--token_id)
* [`token_secret`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--token_secret)
* [`host`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--host)
* [`port`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--port)
* [`ssl_verify`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--ssl_verify)
* [`ssl_ca_file`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--ssl_ca_file)
* [`config_file`](#-proxmox_datacenter_manager--config_file)

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--token_id"></a>`token_id`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^@!\s]+@[^@!\s]+![^!\s]+\z/]`

PDM API token ID in user@realm!tokenname format.

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--token_secret"></a>`token_secret`

Data type: `Sensitive[String]`

PDM API token secret.

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--host"></a>`host`

Data type: `String`

PDM hostname or IP address.

Default value: `'localhost'`

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--port"></a>`port`

Data type: `Integer`

PDM HTTPS API port.

Default value: `8443`

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--ssl_verify"></a>`ssl_verify`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to verify the PDM TLS certificate.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--ssl_ca_file"></a>`ssl_ca_file`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A\//]]`

CA bundle used for PDM certificate verification, or `undef` to use the system trust store.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-proxmox_datacenter_manager--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

Absolute path for the transport configuration. A symlink is created at the provider discovery path when this differs.
Defaults to the agent's own confdir (fact `proxmox_datacenter_manager_confdir`), which is
where the providers look; the compiling server's confdir may differ.

Default value: `"${$facts['proxmox_datacenter_manager_confdir'].lest || { $settings::confdir }}/pdm_transport.yaml"`

### <a name="proxmox_datacenter_manager--resources"></a>`proxmox_datacenter_manager::resources`

This convenience class turns hashes into the corresponding `pdm_*` resources. It does
not configure the provider transport; declare `proxmox_datacenter_manager` before this
class.

#### Examples

##### Declare resources directly

```puppet
class { 'proxmox_datacenter_manager::resources':
  remotes => {
    'production' => {
      type   => 'pve',
      nodes  => ['pve01.example.com'],
      authid => 'pdm@pve!manager',
      token  => Sensitive(lookup('pdm::remotes::production_token')),
    },
  },
}
```

#### Parameters

## Resource types

### <a name="pdm_acl"></a>`pdm_acl`

Titles contain the object path, user/group/token ID, and role separated by pipes.

#### Examples

##### Grant a token the Auditor role

```puppet
pdm_acl { '/|automation@pdm!ci|Auditor':
  ensure    => present,
  propagate => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_acl` type.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the ACL exists.

Default value: `present`

##### `propagate`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether permissions propagate.

Default value: `true`

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_acl` type.

* [`acl_path`](#-pdm_acl--acl_path)
* [`role`](#-pdm_acl--role)
* [`ugid`](#-pdm_acl--ugid)
* [`ugid_type`](#-pdm_acl--ugid_type)

##### <a name="-pdm_acl--acl_path"></a>`acl_path`

namevar

Data type: `String`

ACL object path.

##### <a name="-pdm_acl--role"></a>`role`

namevar

Data type: `String`

PDM role name, e.g. Administrator, Auditor, or NoAccess. PDM ships no API to create custom roles, and the role list is
not enumerated by the API, so this is a free-form string rather than a closed Enum.

##### <a name="-pdm_acl--ugid"></a>`ugid`

namevar

Data type: `String`

User, group, or token ID.

##### <a name="-pdm_acl--ugid_type"></a>`ugid_type`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['user', 'group', 'token']]`

ACL subject type. Inferred from ugid when omitted; token is accepted for imported ACLs.

### <a name="pdm_api_token"></a>`pdm_api_token`

PDM returns a generated token secret only during creation. Set `secret_file` to
retain it on the Puppet agent without exposing it in reports or logs.

#### Examples

##### Create a token and retain its generated secret

```puppet
pdm_api_token { 'automation@pdm!ci':
  ensure      => present,
  enable      => true,
  comment     => 'CI automation',
  secret_file => '/etc/puppetlabs/puppet/pdm-ci-token.secret',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_api_token` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PDM API property names to remove during an update.

##### `enable`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether the token is enabled.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the token exists.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Unix expiry timestamp; 0 means no expiry.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_api_token` type.

* [`secret_file`](#-pdm_api_token--secret_file)
* [`tokenid`](#-pdm_api_token--tokenid)

##### <a name="-pdm_api_token--secret_file"></a>`secret_file`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Agent-local file receiving the one-time token secret on creation, written with mode 0600.

##### <a name="-pdm_api_token--tokenid"></a>`tokenid`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Full token ID in user@realm!tokenname format.

### <a name="pdm_node_config"></a>`pdm_node_config`

The only valid resource title is `localhost`. PDM does not allow this object to be
deleted, so `ensure => absent` performs no deletion; to stop managing it, remove the
resource from the catalog rather than setting `ensure => absent`.

#### Examples

##### Configure node defaults

```puppet
pdm_node_config { 'localhost':
  default_lang => 'en',
  email_from   => 'pdm@example.com',
  http_proxy   => 'http://proxy.example.com:3128',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_node_config` type.

##### `ciphers_tls_1_2`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

TLS 1.2 cipher list.

##### `ciphers_tls_1_3`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

TLS 1.3 ciphersuites.

##### `default_lang`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Default language.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PDM API property names to remove during an update.

##### `email_from`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Sender email.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Always-present object; absent performs no deletion. Remove the resource from the catalog to stop managing it.

Default value: `present`

##### `http_proxy`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

HTTP proxy.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_node_config` type.

* [`node`](#-pdm_node_config--node)

##### <a name="-pdm_node_config--node"></a>`node`

namevar

Data type: `Enum['localhost']`

Singleton node configuration resource.

### <a name="pdm_realm"></a>`pdm_realm`

Both realm secrets are compared on every run. `client_key` is returned by the API,
so it needs no node access; `bind_password` is compared against
`/etc/proxmox-datacenter-manager/access/ldap-passwords.json` and therefore requires
the agent to run on the PDM node as root. See the README.

#### Examples

##### Configure an LDAP realm

```puppet
pdm_realm { 'corp-ldap':
  ensure        => present,
  type          => 'ldap',
  server1       => 'ldap.example.com',
  base_dn       => 'dc=example,dc=com',
  user_attr     => 'uid',
  bind_dn       => 'cn=search,dc=example,dc=com',
  bind_password => Sensitive(lookup('pdm::ldap_bind_password')),
  mode          => 'ldap+starttls',
  verify        => true,
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_realm` type.

##### `acr_values`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID ACR values.

##### `audiences`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID audiences.

##### `autocreate`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Automatically create OpenID users.

##### `base_dn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP/AD base DN.

##### `bind_dn`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP bind DN.

##### `bind_password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

LDAP/AD bind password. Compared against ldap-passwords.json on the PDM node and re-sent when it differs.

##### `capath`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

CA certificate or directory.

##### `client_id`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID client ID.

##### `client_key`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

OpenID client secret. PDM returns it verbatim, so drift is detected over the API without node access.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comment.

##### `default`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Whether this is the default login realm.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PDM API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the realm exists.

Default value: `present`

##### `filter`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP user filter.

##### `issuer_url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID issuer URL.

##### `mode`

Data type: `Optional[Enum['ldap', 'ldap+starttls', 'ldaps']]`

LDAP connection mode.

##### `port`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

LDAP/AD server port.

##### `prompt`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID prompt.

##### `scopes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID scopes.

##### `server1`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Primary LDAP/AD server.

##### `server2`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Fallback LDAP/AD server.

##### `sync_attributes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Attribute mapping.

##### `sync_defaults_options`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Sync defaults.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['ldap', 'ad', 'openid']`

Realm type. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `user_attr`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

LDAP username attribute.

##### `user_classes`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Comma-separated LDAP user object classes.

##### `username_claim`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

OpenID username claim. PDM only accepts it during realm creation.

##### `verify`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

Verify the LDAP server certificate.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_realm` type.

* [`realm`](#-pdm_realm--realm)

##### <a name="-pdm_realm--realm"></a>`realm`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Realm identifier.

### <a name="pdm_remote"></a>`pdm_remote`

The PDM API blanks the remote token on read, so drift is detected against the copy
PDM keeps in `/etc/proxmox-datacenter-manager/remotes.shadow`. Managing `token`
therefore requires the agent to run on the PDM node as root; see the README.

#### Examples

##### Manage a Proxmox VE remote

```puppet
pdm_remote { 'production':
  ensure => present,
  type   => 'pve',
  nodes  => ['pve01.example.com', 'pve02.example.com'],
  authid => 'pdm@pve!manager',
  token  => Sensitive(lookup('pdm::remotes::production_token')),
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_remote` type.

##### `authid`

Data type: `String`

Authentication ID used on the remote.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PDM API property names to remove during an update.

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the remote exists.

Default value: `present`

##### `nodes`

Data type: `Array[String, 1]`

Cluster node hostnames or IP addresses.

##### `token`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Remote API token secret. Compared against remotes.shadow on the PDM node and re-sent when it differs.

##### `type`

Data type: `Enum['pve', 'pbs']`

Remote product type. Cannot be changed after creation.

##### `web_url`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Web UI URL configuration.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_remote` type.

* [`create_token`](#-pdm_remote--create_token)
* [`id`](#-pdm_remote--id)

##### <a name="-pdm_remote--create_token"></a>`create_token`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Ask PDM to create this token on the remote during creation.

##### <a name="-pdm_remote--id"></a>`id`

namevar

Data type: `String`

Remote ID.

### <a name="pdm_user"></a>`pdm_user`

Passwords are verified with crypt(3) against the hash in
`/etc/proxmox-datacenter-manager/access/shadow.json`, so managing `password`
requires the agent to run on the PDM node as root. See the README.

#### Examples

##### Manage an automation user

```puppet
pdm_user { 'automation@pdm':
  ensure => present,
  enable => true,
  email  => 'automation@example.com',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `pdm_user` type.

##### `comment`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Human-readable comment.

##### `delete_properties`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String]]`

PDM API property names to remove during an update.

##### `email`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Email address.

##### `enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the account is enabled.

Default value: `true`

##### `ensure`

Data type: `Enum[present, absent]`

Whether the user exists.

Default value: `present`

##### `expire`

Data type: `Optional[Integer]`

Unix expiry timestamp; 0 means no expiry.

##### `firstname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

First name.

##### `lastname`

Data type: `Optional[String]`

Last name.

##### `password`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]]`

Account password. Verified against shadow.json on the PDM node and re-sent when it no longer matches.

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `pdm_user` type.

* [`userid`](#-pdm_user--userid)

##### <a name="-pdm_user--userid"></a>`userid`

namevar

Data type: `String`

User ID in user@realm format.
